content.user_title: Scale Python Data Workflows with Dask
content.value_statement: Large Python datasets can exceed local memory and slow pandas or NumPy workflows. This skill guides Dask collections, schedulers, and performance patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Dask DataFrames instead of pandas.
Guides Dask Array chunking for larger-than-memory NumPy workflows.
Shows how Dask Bags process text, JSON, logs, and Python objects.
Describes Futures for dynamic task submission and dependency handling.
Compares thread, process, synchronous, and distributed scheduler choices.
Provides performance guidance for partitions, chunks, persistence, and dashboards.
limitations: It does not install Dask or manage cluster infrastructure.
It cannot verify memory use without runtime metrics.
It focuses on core Dask concepts, not every Dask extension.
Users must adapt examples to their own paths, schemas, and hardware.

use_cases.title: Scale a pandas pipeline
use_cases.description: Convert pandas logic into a Dask DataFrame workflow for large CSV or Parquet datasets.

use_cases.title: Process scientific arrays
use_cases.description: Plan Dask Array chunks and compute steps for large numerical datasets.

use_cases.title: Build custom parallel tasks
use_cases.description: Use Dask Futures for dependent tasks, data scattering, and cluster monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Dask collection
prompt_templates.prompt: I have data shaped like [describe data]. Help me choose between Dask DataFrame, Array, Bag, and Futures.

prompt_templates.title: Convert pandas to Dask
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pandas workflow and explain how to convert it to a Dask DataFrame workflow safely.

prompt_templates.title: Tune chunks and partitions
prompt_templates.prompt: Given my dataset size, memory, core count, and operations, recommend Dask partition or chunk settings.

prompt_templates.title: Design distributed execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Dask Futures workflow with dependent tasks, data scattering, monitoring, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: A user asks whether to use pandas or Dask for many Parquet files larger than memory.
output_examples.output: The response recommends Dask DataFrames, explains lazy evaluation, suggests partition checks, and notes when to persist results.

output_examples.input: A researcher has a large multidimensional array and slow NumPy operations.
output_examples.output: The response explains chunk sizing, warns about unsupported operations, and proposes staged computation.

output_examples.input: A developer wants to run many dependent Python tasks on a cluster.
output_examples.output: The response recommends Dask Futures and describes task submission, data scattering, result gathering, and dashboard monitoring.

best_practices: Load data with Dask readers instead of creating large local pandas or NumPy objects first.
Choose partitions or chunks that balance memory use with scheduler overhead.
Use the Dask dashboard and persist reused intermediates when tuning performance.
anti_patterns: Calling compute repeatedly inside loops instead of computing related results together.
Creating millions of tiny tasks when partition-level work would be more efficient.
Using distributed scheduling before confirming that data size and workload justify it.

faq.question: Does this skill run Dask jobs?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples for writing Dask workflows in your environment.

faq.question: Can it help migrate pandas code?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains DataFrame patterns, lazy execution, partitioning, and common migration issues.

faq.question: Does it cover distributed clusters?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes clients, Futures, dashboards, and scheduler selection at a practical level.

faq.question: Is it only for tabular data?
faq.answer: No. It also covers arrays, unstructured data with Bags, and custom task workflows.

faq.question: Will it choose exact memory settings?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend settings from supplied hardware and dataset details, but validation is still needed.

faq.question: What input details help most?
faq.answer: Provide data size, file format, memory, core count, operations, and expected output format.
